mbm-2801.clue: My quilt folds into its own pocket.
mbm-2801.quote: I made my first travel quilt too long for my bag. Gran showed me how to sew a pocket on the back and tuck the whole thing inside. It's been my pillow on every night train since.

mbm-2802.clue: I got cast because my knees knock.
mbm-2802.quote: I auditioned for the brave guard and my knees made the armor rattle. The director cast me as the nervous palace cook. I got to keep one rattly knee plate and the funniest line in the play.

mbm-2803.clue: Our sofa is a ferry on Sunday mornings.
mbm-2803.quote: We get into pajamas, put on the harbor show and pretend each commercial is a port. My little brother collects the tickets in a cereal bowl. Nobody has ever missed our boat.

mbm-2804.clue: Two small weights keep my music in place.
mbm-2804.quote: I practice with my training log open beside the rack. The smallest plates hold the sheet music flat when the gym fan blows. Between sets I learn another four bars on my harmonica.

mbm-2805.clue: I bought my skis for the scratches.
mbm-2805.quote: An old pair at the ski swap had two dozen shallow scratches by the tips. They belonged to the instructor who taught me as a kid. He grinned when I added the first scratch of my own.

mbm-2806.clue: We made room for a pocketful of stars.
mbm-2806.quote: My sister saved sequins that fell off her recital dress. I tucked them behind a little piece of netting in our quilt. Give the patch a shake and her first dance starts sparkling all over again.

mbm-2807.clue: I keep one bookmark for bad weather.
mbm-2807.quote: When I have to leave a book at the sad chapter I tuck in my yellow umbrella bookmark. The next time I open it someone is already standing by with shelter.

mbm-2808.clue: I buy the map after I get lost.
mbm-2808.quote: I walk until I find a shop with a hand-painted clock, then buy a map and mark the spot. I learned more about that neighborhood asking people the time than I did from the guidebook.

mbm-2809.clue: My pattern starts with an old grocery list.
mbm-2809.quote: I turned the list of weekly vegetables into quilt colors. Carrot orange, spinach green, one surprising aubergine. My dad looked at the finished squares and asked what day dinner was.

mbm-2810.clue: I posed with a paper umbrella in January.
mbm-2810.quote: The drawing group wanted to study reflected light. I held a yellow umbrella under the studio lamp and wore my huge winter coat. Twelve summer pictures came out of one very cold morning.

mbm-2811.clue: The pirate can't take off his hat.
mbm-2811.quote: I glued a feather on my wooden marionette's pirate hat and accidentally fixed the hat to his head. Now he bows by taking off his whole head. It's our most popular trick.

mbm-2812.clue: I once called a whole match from the kitchen.
mbm-2812.quote: My aunt put the smooth side of the bocce court right under her kitchen window. When my ankle kept me indoors I peeled potatoes there and called each point. The losers did the washing up. I've never seen such careful measuring.

mbm-2813.clue: I paint the empty chair first.
mbm-2813.quote: At my aunt's cafe there's one chair beside the door where everyone stops to chat. I painted that chair through three shifts. My sketches filled up with different coats, scarves and hands, but always the same red seat.

mbm-2814.clue: One sleeve is a secret measuring tape.
mbm-2814.quote: I stitched short marks inside my work shirt cuff so I can measure a hem without waking the baby to find my ruler. They stop exactly where he once grabbed my sleeve.

mbm-2815.clue: My paper sea has two speeds.
mbm-2815.quote: Backstage I pull the blue cloth sea left and right while the actors sail. At rehearsal the captain complimented my weather. I gave him a calm crossing and kept my storm for opening night.

mbm-2816.clue: The best part of jump day smells of rosemary.
mbm-2816.quote: After every jump we meet at the landing fence to help our oldest club member empty his pockets. He brings rosemary rolls baked before dawn. On my first solo I opened my hands for the bread and realized they'd finally stopped shaking.

mbm-2817.clue: One paper swallow keeps its feet.
mbm-2817.quote: I was cutting a line of swallows into paper when I left two little tabs hanging from one bird. My brother called it the one about to land. We hung that square just above his doorstep.

mbm-2818.clue: I put the sky on our ceiling.
mbm-2818.quote: I saved the three colors of my first parachute in paint swatches. When we repainted the hall I asked for three narrow stripes over the door. My flatmates duck under them on their way out and call it their morning jump.

mbm-2819.clue: The octopus only wanted seven mittens.
mbm-2819.quote: I crocheted a little octopus for my nephew. When I ran out of wool before the last arm he tucked a pencil into the gap and declared the octopus a writer. I made it a tiny notebook too.

mbm-2820.clue: The first chairlift ride is for listening.
mbm-2820.quote: I go early and sit quietly under the cable's little hum. At one tower it goes up a note. My skiing buddy and I hum that note till we reach the top.

mbm-2821.clue: My oldest quilt has a baked edge.
mbm-2821.quote: I spread it too near the picnic oven years ago and singed one corner. I bound that edge in red cloth. At every reunion somebody asks for the burnt slice of blanket.

mbm-2822.clue: Our map has a button instead of a bridge.
mbm-2822.quote: My father and I pieced the streets from his childhood neighborhood. He couldn't quite remember where the footbridge stood. We fixed a button there so he can move it whenever another old friend visits.

mbm-2823.clue: I took the long way round one syllable.
mbm-2823.quote: My little cousin drew a long winding slide on a card and asked me to sing what it looked like. I started high, slid till the note tickled, and bumped up at the end. We shuffle a stack of her drawings before every singing lesson now.

mbm-2824.clue: My scorecard flies a little paper plane.
mbm-2824.quote: At bowling night my kid folds a plane out of the spare scoresheet. If I catch a tricky spare he sends it down the bench. It has never been on the lane and has a perfect record.

mbm-2825.clue: My brother knows which tune I mean by my elbow.
mbm-2825.quote: When our son group plays I lift my elbow a little for the break in my clave rhythm. My brother sees it from behind his guitar and comes in exactly on time. Our aunt calls it family shorthand.
